symbols.def: \(d(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\).

symbols.name: \mathcal X_{t,P}

symbols.name: g_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(g_{t,P}\) denotes a Borel representative on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\) of the observed-outcome regression equivalence class \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]\) for \(z\in\mathcal A_t\), with equivalence taken under the one-sided restricted score measure. symbols.name: \theta_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)\), the unique trace on the model classes below.

symbols.name: \tau_P
symbols.def: \(\tau_P(x)=\theta_{1,P}(x)-\theta_{0,P}(x)\).

symbols.name: q_{t,P}

symbols.name: \mathsf J_P
symbols.def: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) is the largest cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\{x\in\mathcal B:\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}q_{t,P}(x,h)\le u\}\).

symbols.name: K_P
symbols.def: \(K_P(x,h)=1\vee\mathsf J_P(h,a_P(x,h))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_n

symbols.name: r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

novel.justification: This project-specific global entropy condition is satisfied by smooth compact administrative boundaries, including the circular witnesses, and directly controls the number of boundary locations that every covering and chaining upper bound must handle; it imposes no local Ahlfors measure condition.

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).

standard.name: Lipschitz regression smoothness on the observed design support
bounded Hölder-ball envelope for the regression trace

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the one-sided restricted score measure \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\) on Borel sets \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^2\); there exists a single regular conditional law \(\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\) of the observed \(Y\) given \(X=z\) and, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), a \(\mu_{t,P}\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\subseteq\mathcal X_{t,P}\) such that, simultaneously for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\) and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}\exp\{\lambda(y-g_{t,P}(z))\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\le\exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.

standard.name: centered observed-side conditional sub-Gaussian regression noise; independent-error precedent only, with the restricted-kernel formulation derived here

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The common two-sided boundary modulus is project-specific and is realized by geographic designs whose score density vanishes polynomially with inward normal distance along an administrative boundary; Gaiffas2005Degenerate motivates polynomial design degeneracy only in a one-dimensional pointwise problem.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: The envelope is realized by a single polynomial density zero on an otherwise positive tubular design and formalizes isolated geographic access bottlenecks without restricting response smoothness.
A persistent isolated thin site occurs where a smooth boundary meets one lake, pass, or data-redaction pocket, and the circular witness gives an explicit law with this property.

Boundary-wide sampling depletion arises when residence or measurement density vanishes with normal distance from an entire administrative border, and the symmetric tubular witness realizes the condition exactly.

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: A declared common modulus records the weakest two-sided local information available along the boundary and can be estimated from score-only pilot data in geographic designs.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: A lower packing envelope describes guaranteed multiplicity of sparse boundary segments and is directly realized by repeated tubular depletion.

definitions.name: nonempty triangular profile union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

definitions.name: empirical one-sided counts
definitions.construction: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).

definitions.name: count-adaptive bandwidth
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

definitions.name: expected-sup minimax risk
definitions.construction: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

definitions.name: explicit circular thinning witnesses
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

definitions.name: two-sided scale-dependent tent family
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: arbitrary-modulus optimal-recovery handle
definitions.construction: Use the count-qualified local-constant estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) on \(\mathcal H_n\), clipped to \([-2L,2L]\). Its global upper guarantee is obtained from the lower mass modulus \(m\), empirical one-sided counts \(N_{t,n}\), and global boundary entropy. Its converse uses radius-\(h/3\) Lipschitz tents at \(h\)-separated thin sites certified by \(\mathsf J_{-}\) and finite-information testing inside \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

definitions.name: thickness-adaptive honest-band handle
definitions.construction: Condition on the observed scores and calibrate all nonempty side averages over the finite disk-pattern family by the conditional tail radius supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), whose moment-generating-function bound is derived from the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition; add the Lipschitz bias \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) at a positive selected count and the trace envelope \(L\) at a zero count, then difference the two sides to form \(\mathcal C_n\). For any two full observed laws, transfer simultaneous coverage between them with \(\operatorname{TV}\) to obtain the two-law expected-half-width obstruction. This handle does not perform local multiplicity calibration and does not replace full-observed-law distinguishability by score-only distinguishability.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the target a unique observed-side trace rather than a version-dependent conditional mean at a null boundary point.
statements.gap: HahnToddVanDerKlaauw2001 identifies regression-discontinuity limits under continuity, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance studies the boundary curve; this node records identification on vanishing-support sides without assigning a conditional mean at the boundary itself.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can interpret the fitted jump as an observed-law-identified causal trace contrast even when the score has zero density on the boundary.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).
statements.justification: This calculation is the geometry kill test on which every polynomial-thickness rate depends.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate calibrates rates to a one-dimensional design density, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance does not calculate polynomial horn mass.
statements.consumer: Support diagnostics for geographic boundary designs can translate a measured horn cross-section into the correct effective-sample-size exponent.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\), a vertical section of \(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\) at inward coordinate \(u\) has length \(2u^{\kappa-1}\). Since \(B(0,h)\subset\{0<u<h\}\times[-h,h]\), Tonelli's theorem for the nonnegative section indicator gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \le 2\int_0^h u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
For \(0<u<h/2\), one has \(h^2-u^2\ge3h^2/4\). Because \(\kappa>2\), for all sufficiently small \(h<h_0\),
\[
 u^{\kappa-1}\le(h/2)^{\kappa-1}\le \sqrt{3}h/2.
\]
Hence the entire section \(\{|v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\) lies in \(B(0,h)\), and another application of Tonelli gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \ge 2\int_0^{h/2}u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2^{1-\kappa}}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
Thus one may take \(c_{\kappa}=2^{1-\kappa}/\kappa\) and \(C_{\kappa}=2/\kappa\). Both are positive and finite, and the power is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

statements.statement: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).
statements.justification: The explicit circular laws prove nonemptiness and make the same-modulus, different-multiplicity comparison a legal within-model construction.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 analyze finitely many zeros in univariate regression, but neither supplies two symmetric assignment sides or a boundary-wide circular depletion witness.
statements.consumer: Simulation modules for \(\texttt{rd2d}\) can reproduce both designs from normalized score densities rather than relying on an informal horn sketch.
statements.proof_tex:
Write a point of the circular tube as
\[
 z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi),\qquad |s|\le h_0,\quad 0\le\phi<2\pi.
\]
Because \(h_0<1\), these are nonsingular coordinates with area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\). Hence the pervasive normalizing constant from \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\) is
\[
 Z_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 =2\pi\int_{-h_0}^{h_0}|s|^{\kappa-2}(1+s)\,ds
 =\frac{4\pi}{\kappa-1}h_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
It is positive and finite uniformly for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\). The isolated integrand is nonnegative and bounded by one, so its normalizer is at most \(\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathcal T)<\infty\). On the fixed positive-area subset \(\{z\in\mathcal T:d(z,x_{\star})\ge h_0/2\}\), it is at least \(2^{-(\overline\kappa-2)}\). Hence its normalizer is also bounded uniformly away from zero.

On a sufficiently small coordinate patch about any \(x\in S^1\), let \(s\) be signed normal depth and \(v\) signed arclength. Compactness of \(S^1\) and \(h_0<1\) give constants, uniform in \(x\) and \(\kappa\), for which the Jacobian is bounded above and below and
\[
 c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, on either assignment side and for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(x,h)
 &\asymp \int_0^h\int_{-\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}^{\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}
 s^{\kappa-2}\,dv\,ds\\
 &=h^{\kappa}\int_0^1 2w^{\kappa-2}\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw
 \asymp h^{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The last integral is positive and bounded above and below uniformly on \([2,\overline\kappa]\). Compactness and positivity allow the constants to be enlarged so that (1) holds for every \(0<h\le h_0\). Choose \(c_m>0\) below the uniform lower constant and \(C_m>c_m\) above the uniform upper constant. Every boundary point then belongs to the thin set at level \(C_mh^{\kappa}\). If \(E\) is a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(S^1\), disjoint-arc and covering-arc comparisons with total arclength \(2\pi\) give
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |E|\le C h^{-1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]

For the isolated density put \(s_x=d(x,x_{\star})\). The same coordinate comparison gives, uniformly in the side \(t\),
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c h^{\kappa},&s_x\le2h,\\
 c h^2\min\{1,(s_x/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\},&s_x>2h.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
For the first line, integrate over a side-specific subball of radius proportional to \(h\) whose distance from \(x_{\star}\) is proportional to \(h\). For the second, use a subball of radius \(h/2\) about \(x\) and the triangle inequality. Since \(s_x>2h\) in the second line and \(h_0<1\), both lines are at least a uniform constant times \(h^{\kappa}\). At \(x=x_{\star}\), polar integration on either side also yields
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x_{\star},h)
 \le C\int_0^h r^{\kappa-2}r\,dr
 \le C'h^{\kappa}. \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the common polynomial lower-mass condition and the asserted equivalence at \(x_{\star}\).

If \(a_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\le u\), equation (3) implies, after enlarging a uniform constant to cover the case in which the right-hand side exceeds the circle's diameter,
\[
 s_x\le C\left\{h+(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
An arc of the length on the right-hand side of (5) contains at most
\[
 C\left\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}
\]
points separated by \(h\). This is \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}\). At \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\), this upper bound is constant, while (4) puts \(x_{\star}\) in the thin set. Hence
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1. \tag{6}
\]
The estimates extend to the remaining compact range of radii by changing constants. The circle satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) by the same arc argument. The exponent in (1) and (4) also agrees with \(\mathrm{lem:polynomial\text{-}horn\text{-}mass}\).

Finally, the assignment is sharp by construction and the displayed observed-outcome equation gives consistency. For either witness the kernel
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,dy)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)(dy)
\]
is a single regular conditional law of observed \(Y\) given \(X=z\). On each side, \(g_{t,P}(z)=0\), so for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), and with the empty null set,
\[
 \int |y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty,
 \quad
 \int \{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0,
 \quad
 \int e^{\lambda\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
\]
Thus the corrected observed-side condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) holds exactly. Both observed-side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz and trace-envelope properties hold. Equations (1)--(6) and the class definitions prove
\[
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]

statements.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).
statements.justification: This lemma certifies the packed lower experiment inside the same classes used by the upper bounds and states its pairwise information budget.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate uses local univariate bumps, while the present family perturbs both identified boundary sides at many separated sites without changing the common score-mass modulus.
statements.consumer: The minimax lower theorem can invoke a concrete Fano family for pervasive thinning and a concrete Le Cam pair for isolated thinning.
statements.proof_tex:
The distance map \(z\mapsto d(z,x_j)\) is one-Lipschitz. Thus \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, and each perturbed side regression in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz. Its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/4\le L\) because \(0<h\le h_0/6<1\). The perturbation changes neither the score law nor any local-mass or packing property. The sharp-assignment and consistency properties follow directly from the construction.

Conditionally on \(X=z\), the observed outcome is Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\) and mean \(g_{t,P}(z)\) on side \(t\). Consequently a single regular conditional kernel is
\[
 \mathsf R_P(z,dy)=\mathcal N(g_{T(z),P}(z),\sigma^2)(dy),
 \qquad T(z)=\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}.
\]
For the one-sided restricted measure \(\mu_{t,P}\), one has \(T(z)=t\) almost everywhere, and hence the three integrability, centering, and moment-generating-function requirements in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) hold with equality and empty side-null sets. Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the class definitions put every pervasive perturbation in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

Maximality of the \(3h\)-separated set implies that arcs of radius \(3h\) cover \(S^1\), while arcs of radius \(3h/2\) about its points are disjoint. Comparing their total arclength with \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\le C h^{-1}. \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=Lh/4\). Conditional on \(X=z\), the relevant Gaussian coordinates under alternatives \(j\) and \(k\) have common variance \(\sigma^2\), and their mean difference has absolute value \(a|\psi_{j,h}(z)-\psi_{k,h}(z)|\). Direct integration of the Gaussian density gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2),\mathcal N(\nu,\sigma^2)\}
 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}
\]
The integrand vanishes outside \(B(x_j,h)\cup B(x_k,h)\). The coordinate calculations in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) give
\[
 \int_{B(x_j,h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa},
 \qquad
 \int_{B(x_{\star},h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\), conditioning on \(X\) in (8), and summing the two potential-outcome coordinates if the superpopulation experiment is used, gives in either family
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h},\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h})
 \le \frac{Ca^2h^{\kappa}}{\sigma^2}
 \le \frac{CL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{9}
\]
The observed-data divergence is no larger, by marginalization. For the displayed product measures, likelihood ratios factor by the definition of a product law, so relative entropy is additive. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\otimes n},
 \mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\otimes n})
 \le \frac{CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{10}
\]
At an active center, \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\). The trace formulas in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) yield
\[
 \theta_{1,P}(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \tau_P(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{2}.
\]
Together with (7) and (10), these are all the asserted properties.

statements.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
statements.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.
statements.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\), define the finite one-sided score measure \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\). If \(P\) is in either stated class, \(x\in\mathcal B\), and \(r>0\), set \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). The polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge c_ms^\kappa>0. \tag{18}
\]
Thus every boundary point lies in \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). Lipschitz continuity of the distinguished regression representative and the definition of the trace imply
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x),\qquad t\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\mathcal B. \tag{19}
\]
The partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and the definition of \(T\) make \(X\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T=t\), so the side averages used below estimate the observed-law functional in (19). Consistency, which is a member property of both classes, supplies its causal interpretation as \(\tau_P\).

We first prove the lower bounds by experiments lying in the very classes over which risk is taken. Start from any member of the nonempty class at issue, retain its score law and geometry, take independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and set \(Y(s)=\sigma Z_s\). Call the resulting law \(Q_0\). It remains in the same class: every design condition is unchanged, the side regressions and traces are zero, and the single observed-outcome kernel is \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), which satisfies each restricted-side integrability, centering, and MGF clause in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\).

For the isolated class set \(h=a_0n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\). The isolated thin-site property supplies \(x_h\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_h\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 q_{t_h,Q_0}(x_h,h)=a_{Q_0}(x_h,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{20}
\]
Let \(\psi_h(z)=(1-3d(z,x_h)/h)_+\) and \(\eta_h=Lh/12\). If \(t_h=1\), add \(\eta_h\psi_h(X)\) to \(Y(1)\); if \(t_h=0\), subtract it from \(Y(0)\); leave the other potential outcome unchanged. Since \(\eta_h\psi_h\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, is bounded by \(L\), and changes neither the score law nor the centered Gaussian observed residual kernel, the resulting law \(Q_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\). By (19),
\[
 \|\tau_{Q_1}-\tau_{Q_0}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h. \tag{21}
\]
Direct Gaussian likelihood-ratio integration and (20) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 =\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}\int\psi_h(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_h,Q_0}(z)
 \le \frac{nC_mL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{288\sigma^2}. \tag{22}
\]
Choose \(a_0>0\) so the last expression is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), with supremum distance and \(2\delta=\eta_h\), yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}})\ge c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{23}
\]

For the pervasive class set \(h=a_0(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). Its thin-site property supplies an \(h\)-separated set \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) with
\[
 M\ge c_Jh^{-1},\qquad a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{24}
\]
At each \(x_j\), choose a side attaining the minimum and perturb that side by a radius-\(h/3\), height-\(Lh/12\) tent, with the sign chosen to increase the contrast. Exactly as above, the resulting \(Q_j\) lie in \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Their target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(Lh/12\), because every other tent vanishes at \(x_j\). The calculation in (22) gives
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le M}\operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le Cnh^{\kappa+2}=Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n. \tag{25}
\]
Equation (24) implies \(\log M\ge c_\kappa\log n\) eventually. Taking \(a_0\) sufficiently small makes (25) at most \(a\log M\), where \(a<1/8\) is the constant in \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\). Its multiple-law clause yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}=c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{26}
\]
The exact centered-Gaussian circular experiments of \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) give explicit witnesses to the same information budgets.

For the upper bounds, let \(s_n\) denote the rate claimed for the class at issue. Choose \(b\in\mathcal H_n\) so that, for all large \(n\),
\[
 s_n\le b<2s_n,\qquad b/2\in\mathcal H_n,\qquad b\le h_0/2. \tag{27}
\]
Take a deterministic maximal \(b/2\)-separated boundary net \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\). Global boundary entropy gives \(M\le2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}\). Let \(j(x)\) be the least net index within \(b/2\) of \(x\), define the radius-\(b\) side counts \(K_{t,j}\) and means \(\bar g_{t,j}\), and use the single data-driven estimator
\[
 \widetilde\tau_{n,b}(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\bar g_{1,j(x)}-\bar g_{0,j(x)}\}. \tag{28}
\]
It is measurable in the sample and known geometry. Projection cannot increase the error because \(|\tau_P(x)|\le2L\). On \(K_{t,j(x)}>0\), every included score lies within \(3b/2\) of \(x\), so (19) and Lipschitz smoothness give conditional bias at most \(3Lb/2\).

If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)\le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n\le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{29}
\]
For the pervasive rate, polynomial lower mass, (29), and a union bound over the net and two sides give an event \(H_b\) on which all \(K_{t,j}\ge nc_mb^\kappa/2\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le Cb^{-1}e^{-cnb^\kappa}. \tag{30}
\]
Conditional on the scores, independent sampling factorizes the single observed-outcome kernels, and the corrected restricted-side MGF clauses apply at every selected score. Hence \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) gives conditional expected maximum normalized residual sum at most \(C\sqrt{\log(en)}\). Therefore, on \(H_b\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \max_{t,j}|\bar g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\bar g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{nc_mb^\kappa}}\le C_\kappa b, \tag{31}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(nb^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n\). The clipped loss is at most \(4L\) on \(H_b^c\); equations (30)--(31) and the bias bound prove the pervasive upper rate.

For the isolated rate, \(nb^\kappa\asymp b^{-2}\). Fix a side, take \(D\ge C_m\), put \(u_\ell=\min\{1,D2^\ell b^\kappa\}\), and group net centers by \(q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_0\) or \(u_{\ell-1}<q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_\ell\). Such centers obey \(a_P(z_j,b/2)\le u_\ell\). They are \(b/2\)-separated, so the isolated upper profile gives
\[
 M_\ell\le C_\kappa\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}. \tag{32}
\]
In group zero the mean count is at least \(cb^{-2}\), and in group \(\ell\ge1\) it is at least \(c2^\ell b^{-2}\). Summing (29) with (32) over groups and sides produces an event \(H_b\) on which every group-\(\ell\) count is at least \(c2^\ell b^{-2}\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le C_\kappa\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-c2^\ell/b^2}
 \le C_\kappa e^{-c_\kappa/b^2}. \tag{33}
\]
The same conditional MGF factorization gives, for \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{
 \max_{t,j}|\bar g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\bar g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)|>zb
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le C_\kappa\sum_{\ell\ge0}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cz^22^\ell}. \tag{34}
\]
For all sufficiently large fixed \(z\), the series is at most \(C_\kappa e^{-c_\kappa z^2}\). Integrating this tail shows that the conditional expected stochastic maximum on \(H_b\) is at most \(C_\kappa b\). The bias bound, (33), and the \(4L\) clipped-loss bound off \(H_b\) prove the isolated upper rate.

Thus the estimator (28) witnesses both minimax upper bounds, while (23) and (26) prove the matching lower bounds. Finally,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The common scalar lower modulus therefore cannot determine expected-sup risk; the declared thin-site multiplicity separates the two frontiers.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \asymp (\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
statements.justification: This gives a single count-qualified estimator uniformly over the maximal polynomial lower-mass class, retains the pervasive packing converse, and closes both base and pervasive minimax frontiers when the pervasive subclass is nonempty.
statements.gap: Positive-density and finitely-degenerate univariate sup-norm results do not provide a two-sided vanishing-mass boundary estimator uniform over this base class or the same-modulus pervasive converse.
statements.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths throughout the base class without knowing \(\kappa\), with a specified safe fallback.
statements.proof_tex:
The complementary assignment regions and the definition of \(T\) imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\). The definitions of the empirical counts, local-constant fits, admissible sets, deterministic tie break, and fallback show that \(\widehat\tau_n\) is a single measurable map of \(\mathcal D_n\), the known geometry, \(L\), \(\sigma\), and \(n\). In particular, it uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density.

Fix \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and put
\[
 r=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid in \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\) contains \(h_*\) satisfying \(r\le h_*<2r\). Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_J\) be a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Maximality makes it an \(h_*/2\)-net, and the upper half of \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), inherited through \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), gives
\[
 J\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}. \tag{35}
\]
For every net center and side, the polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 q_{t,P}(z_j,h_*/2)\ge c_m(h_*/2)^\kappa. \tag{36}
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the associated count is binomial. If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E(2^{-N})
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{37}
\]
Taking a union bound over (35), the two sides, and (36), and then using \(B(z_j,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\) whenever \(d(x,z_j)\le h_*/2\), produces a score-measurable event \(G_n\) on which
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,h_*)
 \ge c n c_mh_*^\kappa, \tag{38}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}P(G_n^c)
 \le Ch_*^{-1}\exp\{-c n c_mh_*^\kappa\}. \tag{39}
\]
Because \(h_*\asymp r\),
\[
 \frac{nh_*^\kappa}{\log(e+n/h_*)}
 \ge c\left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\overline\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty \tag{40}
\]
uniformly over the declared exponent range. Hence (38) makes \(h_*\) admissible for every \(x,t\) on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), (38), and \(nr^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)
 +\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}
 {N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}\\
 &\qquad\le Lh_*+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_*)}{c n c_mh_*^\kappa}}
 \le Cr.
 \end{aligned} \tag{41}
\]

The lower-mass condition also supplies the support premise needed at the boundary. For any \(x\in\mathcal B\), side \(t\), and radius \(s>0\), taking \(b=\min\{h_0,s/2\}\) gives
\[
 P_X\{X\in\mathcal A_t:d(X,x)<s\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,b)\ge c_mb^\kappa>0. \tag{42}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\). The Lipschitz member property and the trace definition yield
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{43}
\]
For a nonempty selected averaging set, every included score lies within \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) of \(x\), so (43) bounds its conditional bias by \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\).

Let \(Z_n\) be the maximum of the normalized residual sums over the nonempty disk patterns in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\). That lemma, which was proved above from the corrected observed-side kernel condition, and \(|\mathcal H_n|\le 2+\log_2 n\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{44}
\]
Because \(h\le h_0<1\) entails \(\log(e+n/h)\ge\log n\), equations (41), (43), and (44), followed by the triangle inequality over the two sides, give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]\mathbf 1_{G_n}
 \le Cr\mathbf 1_{G_n}. \tag{45}
\]

On \(G_n^c\), a selected set is either nonempty or is the \(h_0\)-fallback. If it is nonempty, (43), Lipschitzness, and \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0\) bound its conditional mean error by \(Lh_0\); if it is empty, the fit is zero and the bounded-trace member property bounds the trace error by \(L\). Since every nonempty count is at least one, (44) therefore gives the conditional bound \(C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}\) for the supremum loss. The right-hand side of (39) decreases faster than any power uniformly in \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), by (40). Integrating (45) and the off-event bound proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le Cr. \tag{46}
\]

For the fallback probability, repeat the net argument with the fixed radius \(h_0/2\). The net has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}h_0^{-1}\) points, while every center-side count has expectation at least \(nc_m(h_0/2)^\kappa\), which uniformly exceeds \(16\log(e+n/h_0)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Equation (37), a union bound, and ball inclusion imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le C\exp\{-c n c_mh_0^\kappa\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_mh_0^\kappa\}. \tag{47}
\]
The off-event calculation above already includes this event's contribution.

Finally, \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) by \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\). The single-estimator bound (46) gives both \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})\le Cr\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le Cr\). The pervasive converse in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), certified by \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), gives \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr\). When the pervasive subclass is nonempty, monotonicity of minimax risk under class inclusion gives
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \ge R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr. \tag{48}
\]
Equations (46)--(48) establish both matched frontiers.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
statements.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.
statements.proof_tex:
Positivity follows from the strictly positive integrand in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\). With the substitution \(s=u^{-\alpha}\),
\[
 m_\alpha(h)=\frac2\alpha\int_{h^{-\alpha}}^\infty e^{-s}s^{-1/\alpha-1}\,ds.
\]
Let \(a=1+1/\alpha\) and \(x=h^{-\alpha}\). Integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds
 =e^{-x}x^{-a}-a\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a-1}\,ds.
\]
The last integral is between zero and \(x^{-1}\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds\). Hence the ratio of the first integral to \(e^{-x}x^{-a}\) lies between \((1+a/x)^{-1}\) and one and tends to one. Therefore
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\sim\frac2\alpha h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}
 \qquad(h\downarrow0).
\]
This proves the asserted two-sided asymptotic order.

For all sufficiently large \(n\), choose
\[
 h_n=\left(\tfrac12\log n\right)^{-1/\alpha}.
\]
Then \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(e^{-h_n^{-\alpha}}=n^{-1/2}\), and the preceding equivalence gives
\[
 \frac{n m_\alpha(h_n)}{\log n}
 \asymp n^{1/2}(\log n)^{-(\alpha+1)/\alpha-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus a fixed positive exponential modulus admits a vanishing bandwidth with diverging effective sample size and does not by itself force order-one risk.

statements.statement: For a declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), does there exist a data-measurable band \(\mathcal C_n\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma-o(1)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=O(1)\)? Prove the matching honest-width lower bound: every band sequence satisfying the displayed coverage condition obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\ge c\) for a universal \(c>0\). If the upper target is impossible, characterize exactly which pairs \((\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) and \((\kappa',\mathsf J'_{-},\mathsf J'_{+})\) in \(\Lambda_n\), separated by their \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) benchmark functions, must satisfy uniform score-law distinguishability \(\inf_{P,P'}\operatorname{TV}(P_X^{\otimes n},(P'_X)^{\otimes n})\to1\), where \(P\) and \(P'\) range over the corresponding two profile-restricted component classes.
statements.justification: The geometry-general construction gives finite-sample simultaneous coverage on every declared nonempty triangular union, and the two-full-observed-law inequality gives a geometry-general pointwise obstruction; only the matched pervasive and base global expected-sup width frontier is specialized to the certified circular polynomial classes. The uniformly local oracle-width ratio, its matching converse, and an exact score-law criterion remain unresolved.
statements.gap: Global calibration retains a logarithmic penalty where local multiplicity can be bounded, and score-law distance does not by itself control the full observed-law perturbations required by the width argument.
statements.consumer: Future work should calibrate to observable local multiplicity and determine when profile components permit compatible outcome perturbations with controlled full-law distance.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ's lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.
statements.justification: This theorem gives an explicit same-class polynomial witness for which a constant declared lower packing profile nevertheless has the pervasive logarithmic minimax rate.
statements.gap: An exact arbitrary-modulus frontier for a refined class with upper as well as lower thin-site packing control remains unresolved; the frozen two-argument class cannot express the isolated side of that comparison.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow must not interpret a constant lower packing declaration as evidence of isolated thinning; it needs an upper-profile certificate before using an isolated-rate guarantee.
statements.proof_tex:
All statements below concern the independent product experiment in \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\). First, the displayed declarations are well typed. Since \(\kappa>2\) and \(c_m>0\), the map \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) is positive and nondecreasing on \((0,h_0]\). The constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) admit a circular member satisfying \(c_mh^\kappa\le q_{t,P}(x,h)\le1\) at every admissible radius, so \(m(h)\in(0,1]\). The declared map \(\mathsf J_{-}\) takes values in \(\mathbb N_0\) and is nondecreasing in its second argument.

We next prove the two class inclusions. Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\). By \(\mathrm{def:isolated\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), \(P\) has all sharp-assignment, consistency, boundary-entropy, Lipschitz, bounded-trace, and corrected observed-side conditional sub-Gaussian properties required by \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\). Its polynomial lower-mass property gives, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\),
\[
 q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_mh^\kappa=m(h). \tag{66}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:minimum\text{-}side\text{-}mass}\) and the definition of \(\mathsf J_P\), if \(u\le u'\), then
\[
 \{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u\}
 \subseteq
 \{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u'\},
 \qquad
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u'). \tag{67}
\]
If \(u<C_mh^\kappa\), then \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\). If \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\), equation (67) and \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}site}\) give
\[
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)
 \ge\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 \ge1
 =\mathsf J_{-}(h,u). \tag{68}
\]
Equations (66)--(68), together with \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\), prove \(P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Now fix \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\). The same base-class argument proves (66). If \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\), equation (67) and \(\mathrm{ass:pervasive\text{-}thin\text{-}sites}\) give
\[
 \mathsf J_P(h,u)
 \ge\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 \ge c_Jh^{-1}>0.
\]
Because \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\in\mathbb N_0\), strict positivity implies \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\ge1=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\); below the threshold the declared lower profile is zero. Hence
\[
 \mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}). \tag{69}
\]
The circular membership lemma supplies a member of each subclass, so all classes used below are nonempty.

For law classes \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal P\), \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\) gives, for every estimator \(\widetilde\tau_n\) measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ge
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|.
\]
Taking the infimum over the identical estimator set on both sides proves
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P)\ge R_n(\mathcal Q). \tag{70}
\]
Apply (70) to the pervasive inclusion in (69), and then apply the pervasive lower bound from \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\). Its nonemptiness and circular-geometry premises are supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and its partition premise is the assumed equality \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Thus there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \ge R_n(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \ge c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{71}
\]

For the reverse inequality, set
\[
 s_n=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
Then \(s_n\downarrow0\), \(ns_n\to\infty\), and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the grid in \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\) contains a point \(h_n\) such that
\[
 s_n\le h_n<2s_n,
 \qquad h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n. \tag{72}
\]
Indeed, take the numerically smallest grid point no smaller than \(s_n\). Since \(h_0/n<s_n<h_0/2\) eventually, this point is neither endpoint of the grid, and its dyadic predecessor is \(2h_n\). From (72), \(m(h_n)=c_mh_n^\kappa\), and \(\log(e+n/h_n)\le C_0\log n\) for a fixed \(C_0<\infty\) eventually, we obtain
\[
 \frac{nm(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}
 \ge\frac{c_mns_n^\kappa}{C_0\log n}
 =\frac{c_m}{C_0}
 \left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\kappa+2)}
 \longrightarrow\infty. \tag{73}
\]
Thus (73) eventually implies the count qualification in \(\mathrm{thm:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}two\text{-}sided\text{-}bracket}\). Evaluate that theorem's explicit clipped count-adaptive estimator at the feasible bandwidth \(h_n\). Equations (72)--(73) imply constants \(C_1,C_2,C_3<\infty\), independent of \(n\), for which
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\quad\le C_1\left\{Lh_n+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_n)}{nm(h_n)}}\right\}\\
 &\quad\le C_2\left\{s_n+
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{ns_n^\kappa}}\right\}
 =C_3s_n,
 \end{aligned} \tag{74}
\]
where the last equality uses \(s_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n/n\). This clipped count-adaptive estimator is a single estimator measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry, and it does not depend on the member law \(P\). It is therefore an admissible competitor in \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\), so (74) gives
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C_3s_n
 =C_3r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{75}
\]
Combining (71) and (75) proves the asserted matched pervasive rate on the lower-profile-only class.

Finally,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =\frac{(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}}{n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{76}
\]
If the one-site lower declaration recovered the isolated frontier, the risk would be bounded above by a constant multiple of \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), contradicting (71) and (76). The generic-class certificate is the entire pervasive circular subclass retained by (69), not merely a single law. Hence a class constrained only by the scalar lower-mass modulus and a lower packing declaration cannot distinguish isolated from pervasive thinning. An upper thin-site packing restriction or an intrinsic two-sided profile is required for a formulation that separates the two regimes.

statements.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.
statements.proof_tex:
For the two-law assertion, let an estimator induce a nearest-point test \(\widehat J\in\{0,1\}\). On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), the triangle inequality and \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_0,v_1)\ge2\delta\) imply \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge\delta\). The smallest average testing error is
\[
 \frac12\int \min(dQ_0,dQ_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2. \tag{11}
\]
For every measurable event \(A\), the log-sum inequality for the partition \(\{A,A^c\}\) gives, with \(p=Q_1(A)\) and \(q=Q_0(A)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
 \ge2(p-q)^2. \tag{12}
\]
The last inequality follows by integrating the second derivative \(1/\{p(1-p)\}\ge4\) of the binary relative entropy as a function of \(p\), whose value and first derivative vanish at \(p=q\). Taking the supremum over \(A\) in (12) yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)/2}\le1/4.
\]
Equation (11) and the nearest-point implication therefore make the maximum risk at least \(3\delta/8\).

For \(M\ge2\), let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), draw \(Z\) from \(Q_J\), and put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\). Expansion of the logarithms gives, for any dominating law \(Q\),
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q)
 =\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 +(M+1)\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q). \tag{13}
\]
Taking \(Q=Q_0\) in (13) bounds the mutual information by
\[
 I(J;Z)=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \le\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \le a\log M. \tag{14}
\]
For any decoder, if \(p_e=\Pr(\widehat J\ne J)\), conditioning entropy first on the error indicator and then, on error, on at most \(M\) alternatives gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le\log2+p_e\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\) and \(I(J;Z)=H(J)-H(J\mid Z)\), (14) implies
\[
 p_e\ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-a\log M-\log2}{\log M}. \tag{15}
\]
For \(M\ge2\) and \(0<a<1/8\), the right side has a positive numerical lower bound. Nearest-point decoding again implies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_J)\ge\delta\) on error. Averaging over \(J\), then bounding the average risk by the maximum risk, proves the stated conclusion. The argument concerns only the supplied laws, so replacing each by its product experiment leaves it unchanged.

statements.statement:
Let \(M\ge2\), let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws on a common measurable space, and suppose \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)<\infty\) for every \(j\). For every decoder \(\widehat J\) taking values in \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\),
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)-\log2}{\log M}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), and, conditionally on \(J=j\), let the observation \(Z\) have law \(Q_j\). Put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\) and
\[
 p_e=\Pr\{\widehat J(Z)\ne J\}.
\]
Since every \(Q_j\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(Q_0\), all laws are dominated by \(Q_0\). Direct expansion of the logarithms gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 &=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
   +\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q_0)\\
 &\ge \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 =I(J;Z),
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
where the inequality is the nonnegativity of relative entropy, obtained from \(u\log u-u+1\ge0\) after integration. Let \(E=\mathbf 1\{\widehat J(Z)\ne J\}\). Because \(E\) is determined by \((J,Z)\), the entropy chain rule gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)=H(E\mid Z)+H(J\mid E,Z).
\]
The binary entropy is at most \(\log2\). Conditional on \(E=0\), the value of \(J\) is determined by \(Z\); conditional on \(E=1\) and \(Z\), at most \(M\) values remain possible. The entropy of a distribution on at most \(k\) points is at most \(\log k\), by concavity of \(-u\log u\). Consequently,
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le\log2+p_e\log M. \tag{2}
\]
On the other hand, uniformity of \(J\) and the definition of mutual information imply
\[
 H(J\mid Z)=\log(M+1)-I(J;Z). \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), rearranging, and observing that \(\log M>0\) proves the displayed inequality. Finally, the definition of the joint experiment gives
\[
 p_e=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\{\widehat J\ne j\},
\]
which completes the proof.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a score vector outside the \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-null set on which either a conditional-kernel assertion or the conditional product factorization below fails.

For the deterministic trace count, membership of a fixed point \(X_i\) in a closed disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}X_i+s\ge \lVert X_i\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad s=r^2-\lVert c\rVert_2^2. \tag{11}
\]
Thus every disk trace on \(\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}\) is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\). Any trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict without changing the trace: if a point is excluded, its distance from the closed disk is positive and the radius may be increased by less than the minimum of these finitely many positive distances; if no point is excluded, any sufficiently small increase works. Hence equality in (11) creates no additional trace.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\). Adding the last hyperplane retains the old cells and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) of them, because the induced arrangement on that hyperplane has dimension \(v-1\). Therefore
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),
 \qquad A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1. \tag{12}
\]
Induction and Pascal's identity yield
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{13}
\]
Restricting to genuine disks of a fixed radius, restricting their centers to \(\mathcal B\), and intersecting a trace with the fixed side set \(\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t\}\) cannot increase the number of traces. There are two sides and \(|\mathcal H_n|\) radii by \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), so
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{14}
\]

If \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\), both stochastic conclusions follow from the stipulated zero-maximum convention. Suppose otherwise. By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), regular conditional laws of the observations given \((X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) factor for \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector; consequently the residuals are conditionally independent. The definition \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_1\}\) and the partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) give \(T_i=t\) for every index in a side-\(t\) candidate set. Moreover, the restricted score measure gives full mass to its closed support \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\): its complement is a countable union of rational basic open sets of restricted mass zero. After removing the two null sets declared in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), that assumption therefore gives, for every relevant index and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\{e^{\lambda\varepsilon_i}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}
 &=\int_{\mathbb R}
 e^{\lambda\{y-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}}\,\mathsf R_P(X_i,dy)\\
 &\le e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{15}
\]
The same assumption supplies conditional integrability and zero conditional mean. This is precisely the corrected single-kernel, restricted-measure formulation; no Gaussian equality is used.

For nonempty \(S\in\mathscr S_n\), put
\[
 Z_S=\frac1{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i.
\]
Conditional independence and (15) imply, for every \(u\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\{e^{uZ_S}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}
 \le\prod_{i\in S}e^{u^2/(2|S|)}=e^{u^2/2}. \tag{16}
\]
Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{zZ_S}\) and then to \(e^{-zZ_S}\) gives
\[
 \Pr_P\{|Z_S|>z\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\}\le2e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
A union bound over \(S\), which requires no independence among the set-indexed sums, proves
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}. \tag{17}
\]

Finally let \(z_0=\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}\). Since \(|\mathscr S_n|\ge1\), one has \(z_0>1\). The tail-integral identity for nonnegative random variables, (17), and
\[
 \int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\le z_0^{-1}e^{-z_0^2/2}
\]
give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 &\le z_0+2|\mathscr S_n|\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\\
 &\le z_0+z_0^{-1}\le z_0+1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Together with the empty-family case, this is the claimed expectation bound with \(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|\).

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.
statements.justification: This theorem gives an explicit count-based global upper map and a legal same-class Lipschitz-tent converse indexed by the declared lower packing profile.
statements.gap: The two sides match in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes. For arbitrary declarations they can differ because \(\mathsf J_{-}\) may be slack while the upper argument covers the full boundary using global entropy.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can check the sufficient count condition before fitting and report a lower testing experiment when uniform consistency is impossible.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), and write \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\). If \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(r>0\), and \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\), positivity of \(m\) and the declared lower-mass member property in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\) give
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge m(s)>0. \tag{49}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) on both sides. The Lipschitz member property makes the specified representative \(g_{t,P}\) continuous at \(x\), so the definition of the boundary trace gives
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{50}
\]
The complementary assignment and the definition of \(T\) identify each side average with observations having \(T=t\). The bounded-trace member property gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\). Since Euclidean projection onto a closed interval containing the target is nonexpansive, projection cannot increase the pointwise error, and its pointwise loss is at most \(4L\).

For the upper bound, fix \(h\) such that \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and
\[
 nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h). \tag{51}
\]
Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Maximality makes it an \(h\)-net, while \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), and the lower-mass member property,
\[
 N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\sim\operatorname{Bin}\{n,q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\},
 \qquad q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h). \tag{52}
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\), followed by \(1-y\le e^{-y}\), yields
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E(2^{-N})
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq(1-\log 2)/2}
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{53}
\]
Let \(H_h\) be the event that every center-side count is at least \(nm(h)/2\). A union bound over the \(2K\) pairs in (52) gives
\[
 P(H_h^c)\le2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{54}
\]
For each \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose a net center \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\). The triangle inequality gives \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\), and hence, on \(H_h\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)\ge nm(h)/2. \tag{55}
\]
Choose the fixed constant \(A\ge16\). Equations (51) and (55), together with \(\log(e+n/(2h))\le\log(e+n/h)\), show that \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\).

Condition on \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\). The selected bandwidths are then fixed functions of the scores. By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the conditional law is the product of the single observed-outcome kernels. For an index on side \(t\), the corrected restricted-side clause of \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) applies to \(Y_i-g_{t,P}(X_i)\). Consequently, for every deterministic index set \(S\) belonging to one side,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \exp\!\left\{\lambda\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i\right\}
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le \exp\{\sigma^2\lambda^2|S|/2\}. \tag{56}
\]
Thus the disk-pattern count and conditional tail calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) apply. If \(Z_n\) denotes the maximum normalized residual sum appearing there, then
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
 \le\sqrt{2\log\!\left\{4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\right\}}+1
 \le C_0\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{57}
\]
For a nonempty side average at bandwidth \(b\), equation (50) and the Lipschitz member property give conditional bias at most \(Lb\). Its stochastic error is at most \(\sigma Z_n/\sqrt{N_{t,n}(x,b)}\). Since \(b\le h_0<1\) implies \(\log(e+n/b)\ge\log(e+n)\), equation (57) bounds the conditional expected stochastic error uniformly by a constant times the stochastic term in the selection criterion. On \(H_h\), the selected set is nonempty and pointwise minimization of that criterion, followed by comparison with the admissible bandwidth \(2h\) from (55), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C_1\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}. \tag{58}
\]
Here the factor two from the two sides is absorbed into \(C_1\).

Projection, the \(4L\) loss bound on \(H_h^c\), and (54) now yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\quad\le C_2\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 +C_3Lh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{59}
\]
After increasing \(A\) so that \(A/8\ge2\), equation (51) implies
\[
 h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}
 \le h^{-1}(e+n/h)^{-2}
 \le h,
\]
so the final term in (59) is absorbed into the bias term. Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs and combining with the unconditional \(4L\) bound proves the upper display. The definitions of the empirical counts, admissible bandwidths, count-adaptive bandwidth, estimator, and fixed projection show directly that this single data-driven estimator uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the same-class converse. Choose \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), which exists by the theorem's nonemptiness premise, and retain its score marginal and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) and define the observed outcome by consistency. All score-dependent member properties are unchanged, both side regressions and traces vanish, and the single observed-outcome kernel is exactly centered Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\). Thus all member conditions in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\) hold and \(P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

Fix \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and put \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\ge1\). The declared-profile member property and the definition of \(\mathsf J_{P_0}\) supply \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) such that \(a_{P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\). For every \(j\), choose \(t_j\in\{0,1\}\) with \(q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\), and set
\[
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},
 \qquad
 \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+. \tag{60}
\]
Define \(P_j\) by retaining the score law and independent Gaussian noises and setting
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y(1)=\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=\sigma Z_0,&t_j=1,\\
 Y(1)=\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=-\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0,&t_j=0.
 \end{cases} \tag{61}
\]
The perturbation in (61) is \(3\eta_h/h=L/4\)-Lipschitz. Since \(h\le h_0/3<1\), its absolute trace is at most \(\eta_h<L\). It changes neither the score-dependent conditions nor the centered Gaussian observed residual kernel. Therefore every \(P_j\) belongs to \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\); this derives membership from the class conditions rather than assigning it by construction.

At \(x_j\), the target under \(P_j\) equals \(\eta_h\). If \(k\ne j\), the \(h\)-separation of the centers and the radius-\(h/3\) support of the tents imply \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\). Consequently,
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{62}
\]
Only observations with \(X\in\mathcal A_{t_j}\cap B(x_j,h/3)\) have a shifted observed conditional mean. The exact centered-Gaussian likelihood formula and \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 &=\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}
   \int_{\mathcal A_{t_j}}\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,dP_X(z)\\
 &\le\frac{nL^2h^2}{288\sigma^2}
   q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)
 \le\frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{63}
\]
If \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), retain one alternative and choose the universal \(a>0\) so that (63) is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), applied with \(2\delta=\eta_h\), yields minimax risk at least \(cLh\). If instead \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\), use \(\log(M+1)/\log M\le\log3/\log2\) and decrease \(a\) by that universal factor. Then (63) meets the multiple-law hypothesis of the same lemma, and (62) yields
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh. \tag{64}
\]

For a sequence of nonempty classes with moduli \(m_n\), the displayed sufficient condition supplies qualifying \(h_n\) eventually; equation (59) then tends to zero because \(h_n\downarrow0\) and \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\). Conversely, let \(F_n\) be the set of radii for which some \(u\) satisfies either information condition in the lower display. If \(\sup F_n\not\to0\), then along a subsequence there are feasible radii bounded below by a positive constant, and (64) keeps the minimax risk bounded away from zero. This proves the stated necessary condition.

For \(m_\alpha\), \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}\). Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then
\[
 \frac{nm_\alpha(s_n)}{\log(e+n/s_n)}
 \asymp\frac{n^{1/2}s_n^{\alpha+1}}{\log n}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{65}
\]
Round upward to a dyadic \(h_n\in\mathcal H_n\) with \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), this point is not a grid endpoint, so \(2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\); monotonicity of \(m_\alpha\) and \(h_n<2s_n\) preserve (65). Hence the sufficient condition holds for every fixed positive exponential modulus.

Finally, put \(u=C_mh^\kappa\). When \(M\asymp1\), the first information condition balances \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp1\), and therefore gives \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). When \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), the second balances \(nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log(1/h)\), and therefore gives \(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). These lower rates match the two rates in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\). For a slack declaration, the circular pervasive witness can be paired with \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\}\): the declared lower profile then exposes only one site, whereas the global-net upper argument still pays for the full boundary entropy. Thus the arbitrary-profile result is the claimed two-sided bracket and does not assert an unproved exact criterion.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), fix an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), and suppose \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\). For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), and every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
\]
there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the first conclusion, and it obeys the second conclusion whenever widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. These conclusions hold for every such assignment geometry; the circular laws are needed only as explicit nonemptiness witnesses.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose an arbitrary \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), whose existence is the stated nonemptiness premise, and retain its score marginal \(P_X^\circ\) and assignment geometry. On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(Q_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) and by the consistency equation for the observed outcome. The sharp-assignment and consistency conditions hold by construction. The boundary entropy, polynomial lower mass, and pervasive packing conditions depend only on the retained score law and geometry. Both side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz and bounded-trace conditions hold, and the single observed-outcome kernel is exactly centered Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\). Hence every member condition in \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\) holds, and
\[
 Q_0\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{77}
\]

Put \(r_n=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), fix \(a_\gamma=(1-\gamma)/4\), and let \(h=b_\gamma r_n\), where the fixed constant \(b_\gamma>0\) will be chosen below. For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(h\le h_0\).
