The pervasive thin-site condition and the definition of \(\mathsf J_{Q_0}\) provide an \(h\)-separated set \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_M\}\subseteq\mathcal B\) with
\[
 M\ge\lfloor c_Jh^{-1}\rfloor,
 \qquad
 a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{78}
\]
For each \(j\), choose \(t_j\in\{0,1\}\) attaining the minimum in \(a_{Q_0}(x_j,h)\), so that
\[
 q_{t_j,Q_0}(x_j,h)\le C_mh^\kappa. \tag{79}
\]
Set \(\eta=\min\{L/6,1\}\), \(\Delta=\eta h\), and
\[
 \phi_j(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+.
\]
For \(j\ge1\), retain the score law and independent Gaussian noises and define \(Q_j\) by
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y(1)=\Delta\phi_j(X)+\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=\sigma Z_0,&t_j=1,\\
 Y(1)=\sigma Z_1,\quad Y(0)=-\Delta\phi_j(X)+\sigma Z_0,&t_j=0.
 \end{cases} \tag{80}
\]
The perturbed side mean in (80) is \(3\eta\)-Lipschitz, and \(3\eta\le L/2<L\). Also \(0<h\le h_0<1\) implies \(\Delta\le\eta\le L/6<L\). Thus the Lipschitz and bounded-trace conditions hold. All score-dependent conditions are unchanged and, after subtracting the appropriate side mean, the single observed-outcome kernel gives a \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) residual on each restricted side. The same member-by-member verification as in (77) therefore proves
\[
 Q_j\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},\qquad 0\le j\le M. \tag{81}
\]
This membership conclusion is derived from the frozen class conditions and does not use the circular tent family.

The supports of the tents have radius \(h/3\), whereas the centers are \(h\)-separated. Consequently, for \(j\ne k\), \(\phi_j(x_k)=0\), while \(\phi_j(x_j)=1\). Continuity of the Lipschitz side means gives their boundary traces, so
\[
 \tau_{Q_0}(x_k)=0,
 \qquad
 \tau_{Q_j}(x_k)=\Delta\mathbf 1\{j=k\}. \tag{82}
\]
Only observations in \(\mathcal A_{t_j}\cap B(x_j,h/3)\) have a shifted observed conditional mean under \(Q_j\). The conditional Gaussian likelihood formula, (79), and \(0\le\phi_j\le1\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 &=\frac{n\Delta^2}{2\sigma^2}
   \int_{\mathcal A_{t_j}}\phi_j(z)^2\,dP_X^\circ(z)\\
 &\le\frac{n\eta^2h^2}{2\sigma^2}q_{t_j,Q_0}(x_j,h)
 \le \frac{C_m\eta^2}{2\sigma^2}nh^{\kappa+2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{83}
\]
Independent sampling justifies both the product experiment and the additive product-law divergence in (83).

Since \(nh^{\kappa+2}=b_\gamma^{\kappa+2}\log n\), while (78) implies
\[
 \log M\ge \frac{1}{2(\kappa+2)}\log n \tag{84}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), one may choose \(b_\gamma>0\), depending on \(\gamma\) and the fixed class envelopes but not on \(n\), so that
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le a_\gamma\log M. \tag{85}
\]
The explicit entropy-decoding inequality \(\mathrm{lem:explicit\text{-}entropy\text{-}decoding\text{-}bound}\) now yields, for every decoder \(\widehat J\),
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \ge p_n:=\frac{\log(M+1)-a_\gamma\log M-\log2}{\log M}. \tag{86}
\]
Because \(M\to\infty\),
\[
 p_n\longrightarrow1-a_\gamma=\frac{3+\gamma}{4}>\gamma. \tag{87}
\]
In particular, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n\ge(1-\gamma)/2\).

We first obtain the global-width conclusion. Put \(W_n^*=\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\). From the reported intervals at \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\), let \(\widehat J\) be the smallest code index \(j\in\{0,\ldots,M\}\) for which the vector \((\tau_{Q_j}(x_1),\ldots,\tau_{Q_j}(x_M))\) lies in their Cartesian product, using zero if no index qualifies. On the simultaneous-coverage event under \(Q_j\), code \(j\) qualifies. If additionally \(W_n^*<\Delta/2\), no two codes qualify, because (82) makes two distinct codes differ by \(\Delta\) in some coordinate, whereas every reported interval has diameter less than \(\Delta\). Therefore Markov's inequality gives
\[
 Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \le\gamma+\epsilon_n+
 \frac{2\mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n^*}{\Delta}. \tag{88}
\]
If one of these expectations is infinite, the desired bound is immediate. Otherwise, average (88), use (86)--(87), and obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge\frac{\Delta}{2}(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n)
 \ge\frac{\eta b_\gamma(1-\gamma)}4 r_n. \tag{89}
\]
This proves the first conclusion with a constant depending on \(\gamma\), never on \(n\).

For the pointwise conclusion, define another decoder to equal zero if every \(\mathcal C_n(x_k)\) contains zero, and otherwise to equal the smallest \(k\) for which zero is absent. Under \(Q_0\), simultaneous coverage implies correct decoding. Under \(Q_j\), equation (82), simultaneous coverage, and \(W_n(x_j)<\Delta/2\) imply that every inactive interval contains zero while the active interval contains \(\Delta\) and excludes zero. Hence
\[
 Q_0^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne0\}\le\gamma+\epsilon_n,
 \qquad
 Q_j^{\otimes n}\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \le\gamma+\epsilon_n+\frac{2\mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n(x_j)}\Delta. \tag{90}
\]
Average (90), compare with (86), and use (87). For at least one \(j\ge1\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_j}W_n(x_j)
 \ge \frac{M+1}{2M}\Delta(p_n-\gamma-\epsilon_n)
 \ge c_\gamma r_n. \tag{91}
\]

It remains to compare (91) to the declared local benchmark. For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid contains \(\overline h\) with \(h\le\overline h<2h\). Polynomial lower mass, retained by every \(Q_j\), gives
\[
 q_{t,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)\ge c_m\overline h^\kappa,
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\}. \tag{92}
\]
Every \(\overline h\)-separated set counted by \(\mathsf J_{Q_j}(\overline h,a_{Q_j}(x_j,\overline h))\) is an \(\overline h\)-separated subset of the whole boundary. Global boundary entropy and \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}effective\text{-}multiplicity}\) therefore imply
\[
 K_{Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)\le1\vee C_{\mathcal B}\overline h^{-1}. \tag{93}
\]
Insert \(\overline h\) into the infimum in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}oracle\text{-}benchmark}\). Equations (92)--(93), \(\overline h\asymp r_n\), and \(nr_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 r_{n,Q_j}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x_j)
 &\le2L\overline h+
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log\{e(1\vee C_{\mathcal B}\overline h^{-1})/\gamma\}}n
 \left\{q_{0,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)^{-1}
       +q_{1,Q_j}(x_j,\overline h)^{-1}\right\}}\\
 &\le C_\gamma r_n.
 \end{aligned} \tag{94}
\]
Combining (91) and (94) proves the pointwise ratio bound.

Finally, \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) by definition. A band honest over the base class is therefore honest over the pervasive subclass, and the supremum over the base class is no smaller. Thus (89) transfers to the base class. No step used circular geometry; the only geometric facts used were the frozen pervasive packing lower bound and global boundary packing upper bound.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). For any admissible assignment geometry under the preceding premises, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n
\]
obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the global lower bound because \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and it obeys the ratio conclusion when widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. The circular witnesses in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) certify explicit nonemptiness only. Thus, whenever the pervasive class is nonempty, the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive and base classes.

Independently of the preceding pervasive-class conclusions, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Uniform local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union, the corresponding local-ratio converse for unions without a nonempty pervasive component, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion stated only through score-law total variation remain open. The global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can remain bounded at an isolated thin site, and score-law total variation alone does not control the distance between full observed laws.
statements.justification: Conditional sub-Gaussian disk-pattern calibration gives finite-sample simultaneous coverage for arbitrary declared complementary geometries. The geometry-general disjoint-tent construction supplies, at every fixed miscoverage level, both the matched global expected-supremum half-width converse and the local-benchmark ratio converse on every nonempty pervasive component; circular witnesses certify explicit nonemptiness only.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance Theorem 5 gives Gaussian bands under positive-density and stable-Gram conditions, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands supplies anti-concentration and data-selected-resolution calibration, ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest treats scalar bias-aware intervals, and accepted-bank \texttt{stat\_bdd\_uniform\_log\_penalty\_v1} proves an expected-risk rather than band-width frontier. Here finite-sample coverage permits vanishing two-sided boundary mass and the pervasive converse is geometry-general, but uniform local-oracle width achievability on arbitrary triangular unions, a corresponding converse for unions without a pervasive component, and an exact score-law criterion remain open.
statements.consumer: Use the explicit band for finite-sample global coverage on declared unions; when a pervasive component is nonempty, its global width is rate-optimal on that component and the containing base class, while the proved local-benchmark statement is a converse rather than a local-oracle achievability guarantee.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\). By \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\), \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) for at least one \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), and hence it satisfies every member condition in \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\). We first verify the trace relation used by the band. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(s>0\), and put \(b=\min\{h_0,s/2\}\). The polynomial lower-mass member property gives
\[
 P_X\{z\in\mathcal A_t:d(z,x)<s\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,b)\ge c_m b^\kappa>0. \tag{95}
\]
Thus every neighborhood of \(x\) has positive mass under the one-sided restricted score measure, so \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\). The Lipschitz condition \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) makes \(g_{t,P}\) continuous at \(x\) on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). Consequently, the definition of the boundary trace yields
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{96}
\]

Write
\[
 z_n=\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}.
\]
For fixed scores, denote by \(\mathscr S_n\) the disk-pattern family in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\). Its cardinality is at most \(M_n\). Substitution of \(z_n\) into that lemma gives, for \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector,
\[
 \Pr_P\!\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{\left|\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}\right|}
 {\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z_n
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z_n^2/2}\le\gamma. \tag{97}
\]
Here \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the corrected \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) are exactly the sampling and single-kernel restricted-side MGF premises of the established lemma. Complementarity \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and the definition of \(T\) ensure that a side-\(t\) disk pattern contains exactly observations with \(T_i=t\).

Consider the selected side fit at \((x,t)\), and abbreviate
\[
 \widehat h=\widehat h_{t,n}(x),\qquad
 N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h),\qquad
 S=\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le\widehat h\}.
\]
If \(N>0\), then \(S\in\mathscr S_n\), and on the event complementary to that in (97),
\[
 \left|\frac1N\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{t,P}(X_i)\}\right|
 \le \sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}{N}}. \tag{98}
\]
Moreover, (96) and \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) imply
\[
 \left|\frac1N\sum_{i\in S}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le \frac1N\sum_{i\in S}L\,d(X_i,x)\le L\widehat h. \tag{99}
\]
Equations (98)--(99) and \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\) show that the side error is at most \(B_{t,n}(x)\). If \(N=0\), that definition makes the side fit equal to zero, while \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\) gives
\[
 |\widehat g_{t,n}(x;\widehat h)-\theta_{t,P}(x)|\le L=B_{t,n}(x). \tag{100}
\]
Because (97) controls every disk pattern simultaneously, (98)--(100) hold simultaneously for all \(x\in\mathcal B\) and both sides with conditional probability at least \(1-\gamma\). Using \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) and the definition \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\), the triangle inequality gives
\[
 |\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\le B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\qquad(x\in\mathcal B). \tag{101}
\]
Thus the displayed band contains \(\tau_P(x)\) for every \(x\) on this event. Integrating (97) over the scores proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma. \tag{102}
\]
For measurability, each count and numerator is a finite sum of Borel functions of the data and \(x\); \(\mathcal H_n\) is finite; and \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\) specifies both a deterministic tie break and an empty-set value. Hence \(\widehat h_{t,n}\), the selected fits, the radii \(B_{t,n}\), and the two interval endpoints are data measurable.

We next prove the expected-width upper bound. Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), put
\[
 r_n=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}, \tag{103}
\]
and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), choose \(h_*\in\mathcal H_n\) such that \(r_n\le h_*<2r_n\). Such a grid point exists by \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), because \(r_n\downarrow0\), \(r_n<h_0\) eventually, and \(r_n/(h_0 2^{-\lceil\log_2 n\rceil})\to\infty\).

Let \(\mathcal N_*\) be a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). Compactness of \(\mathcal B\) and maximality make \(\mathcal N_*\) an \(h_*/2\)-net, while the boundary-entropy member property gives
\[
 |\mathcal N_*|\le 2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}. \tag{104}
\]
For \(z\in\mathcal N_*\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the proof-intermediate count
\[
 \widetilde N_{t,n}(z)=\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,z)\le h_*/2\}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), this is binomial with success probability
\[
 q_{t,P}(z,h_*/2)\ge c_m(h_*/2)^\kappa. \tag{105}
\]
For \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to the nonnegative variable \(2^{-Z}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{Z\le nq/2\}
 \le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E[2^{-Z}]
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le \exp\{-nq(1-\log2)/2\}\le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{106}
\]
The equality uses the binomial generating function, and the first exponential inequality uses \(\log(1-u)\le-u\) for \(0\le u<1\).

Take the union bound in (106) over (104) and both sides. If \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose \(z\in\mathcal N_*\) with \(d(x,z)\le h_*/2\); then \(B(z,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\). We therefore obtain an event \(G_n\) and constants \(c,C>0\), depending only on the declared envelopes, such that uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,h_*)\ge cnh_*^\kappa,
 \qquad
 P(G_n^c)\le Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^\kappa}. \tag{107}
\]
From (103) and \(h_*\asymp r_n\),
\[
 nh_*^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n,
 \qquad
 \frac{nh_*^\kappa}{\log(e+n/h_*)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{108}
\]
Equations (107)--(108) show that \(h_*\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The minimizing property in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), comparison with \(h_*\), (107), and (108) now imply
\[
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}
 {N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}\le C r_n \quad\text{on }G_n, \tag{109}
\]
simultaneously in \(x,t\). Indeed, the objective at \(h_*\) is bounded by
\[
 Lh_*+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h_*)}{cnh_*^\kappa}}\le C r_n, \tag{110}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(h_*\asymp r_n\) and \(nr_n^{\kappa+2}=\log n\).

The elementary bounds \(|\mathcal H_n|\le 2+\log_2 n\) and \(\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\le Cn^3\) give
\[
 \log(2M_n/\gamma)\le C_\gamma\log n
 \le C_\gamma\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x)), \tag{111}
\]
because \(0<\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\le h_0<1\). On \(G_n\) the selected count is positive, so (109) and (111) give
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}}B_{t,n}(x)\le C_\gamma r_n. \tag{112}
\]
On \(G_n^c\), the definition of \(B_{t,n}\), \(h_0<1\), and \(N\ge1\) in its positive-count branch give the deterministic bound
\[
 \sup_{x,t}B_{t,n}(x)\le L+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)}. \tag{113}
\]
Furthermore, (103), (107), and \(h_*\asymp r_n\) imply
\[
 h_*^{-1}e^{-cnh_*^\kappa}\sqrt{\log(2M_n/\gamma)}=o(r_n), \tag{114}
\]
because \(nh_*^\kappa\) grows as a positive power of \(n\), up to a logarithmic factor, and hence its exponential dominates every polynomial and logarithm. Since the displayed interval has
\[
 W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x), \tag{115}
\]
splitting the expectation over \(G_n\) and \(G_n^c\), then applying (107) and (112)--(114), proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\le
 C_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}. \tag{116}
\]

Now suppose \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), and let a band sequence have simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) on that class, where \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\). All premises of \(\mathrm{lem:geometry\text{-}general\text{-}pervasive\text{-}band\text{-}width\text{-}obstruction}\) hold: the assignment regions are complementary, the geometry satisfies global boundary entropy, and the class definition supplies the base conditions together with pervasive thin sites. That lemma therefore gives, for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\ge
 c_\gamma\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}, \tag{117}
\]
and also
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}\ge c_\gamma. \tag{118}
\]
These conclusions are geometry-general. The role of \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) is only to exhibit one specification for which the pervasive class is nonempty. Since \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\), a band honest over the base class is honest over the pervasive subclass, and its base-class supremum is at least the supremum in (117). Conversely, (116) applies to the displayed band on both the base class and its pervasive subclass. Equations (116)--(117) thus prove its matched global expected-supremum half-width frontier on both classes, while (118) is the asserted local-benchmark converse.

Finally, we prove the two-law inequality independently of pervasive thinning. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\), and for \(j=0,1\) let
\[
 A_j=\{\tau_{P_j}(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\}.
\]
Simultaneous coverage over a class containing \(P_0,P_1\) implies
\[
 P_j^{\otimes n}(A_j)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,\qquad j=0,1. \tag{119}
\]
By the defining variational inequality for total variation of the full observed product laws,
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_1)\ge P_1^{\otimes n}(A_1)
 -\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{120}
\]
Combining (119)--(120) with \(P_0(A_0\cap A_1)\ge P_0(A_0)+P_0(A_1)-1\) gives
\[
 P_0^{\otimes n}(A_0\cap A_1)\ge
 1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}). \tag{121}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval \(\mathcal C_n(x)\) contains both target values, so its half-diameter satisfies
\[
 W_n(x)\ge\frac12|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|. \tag{122}
\]
Multiplying (122) by the indicator of \(A_0\cap A_1\), taking the \(P_0\)-expectation, and using the positive part of (121) proves
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
 \frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
This last argument necessarily compares full observed laws. It does not turn score-law total variation into full-law distinguishability, and the global factor in (111) need not match the bounded local multiplicity term in \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\). Accordingly, the theorem asserts neither local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union nor an exact score-law adaptation criterion.

Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under a known sharp bivariate boundary assignment, with score density permitted to vanish at the boundary.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i)\); potential outcomes supply the causal interpretation and only the realized outcome is observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(T_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_1\}\), with both assignment regions and their common boundary known.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment is deterministic. Each side regression is represented on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\); consistency supplies its compatible potential-outcome interpretation, and its unique Lipschitz trace identifies \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\). One-sided information is measured by \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed-side regressions are estimated by local constants with count-qualified bandwidths, a fixed measurable tie-break, and the explicit fallback \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when no bandwidth is admissible.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x)),\quad \mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\Longrightarrow \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\lesssim(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},\quad \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})\asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4--6 give regular-density uniform estimation, inference, and a distance-estimator minimax lower bound for the boundary curve.

Theorems 1--2 give spatially varying uniform regression rates under inhomogeneous one-dimensional design, and Proposition 1 shows that isolated density zeros can permit local improvement over a naive uniform normalization.
Theorems 1--2 give pointwise minimax rates under regularly and severely varying random-design density, including logarithmically slow consistency for exponential degeneracy.
The paper constructs a local-polynomial Lepski estimator adaptive to unknown pointwise design scarcity and smoothness.

The paper combines Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and data-selected resolution levels for honest adaptive bands.
Theorems 2.1--2.2 derive honest bias-aware scalar intervals and efficiency comparisons from power-renormalized bias and standard-deviation formulas.

tldr: The boundary target is the difference of the unique Lipschitz traces of the two observed-side regression classes on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), so it is an observed-law functional even when conditional means at null boundary points are undefined. A single worst-point thickness modulus does not determine expected-sup difficulty: explicit circular designs have the same two-sided mass order \(h^{\kappa}\), but one has a single \(O(h)\)-arc data desert and the other has \(\asymp h^{-1}\) separated thin sites. The resulting nonempty classes have rates \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), respectively, and a count-qualified estimator matches the pervasive frontier without knowing \(\kappa\). The inference question asks for uniform coverage and expected half-width proportional to the explicit local benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) over a declared nonempty triangular profile union, with total-variation distinguishability characterizing any adaptation obstruction.

project_justification.gap: Distance-based boundary-curve theory assumes positive design density. Existing random-design sup-norm theory provides unknown-density spatial normalization and inhomogeneous bands under positive continuous univariate density, while degenerate-design theory is pointwise, univariate uniform, or global \(L^2\) with finitely many zeros.
